verses.1: There was a roaming Vratya. He roused Prajapati to action.
verses.2: Prajapati beheld gold in himself and engendered it.
verses.3: That became unique, that became distinguished, that became great, that became excellent, that became Devotion, that became holy Fervour, that became Truth: through that he was born.
verses.4: He grew, he became great, he became Mahadeva.
verses.5: He gained the lordship of the Gods. He became Lord.
verses.6: He became Chief Vratya. He held a bow, even that Bow of Indra.
verses.7: His belly is dark-blue, his back is red.
verses.8: With dark-blue he envelops a detested rival, with red he pierces the man who hates him: so the theologians say.
verses.9: He arose and went his way to the eastern region.
verses.10: The Brihat, the Rathantara, the Adityas and all the Gods followed him.
verses.11: That man is alienated from the Brihat, the Rathantara, the Adityas, and all Gods who reviles the Vratya who possesses this knowledge.
verses.12: He who hath this knowledge becomes the beloved home of the Brihat, the Rathantara the Adityas, and all the Gods.
verses.13: In the eastern region Faith is his leman, the hymn his panegyrist, knowledge his vesture, day his turban, night his hair, Indra's two Bays his circular ornaments, the splendour of the stars his jewel.
verses.14: Present and Future are his running footmen, mind is his war-chariot,
verses.15: Matarisvan and Pavamana are they who draw it, Vita is his charioteer, Storm his goad,
verses.16: Fame and Glory are his harbingers. Fame and Glory come to him who hath this knowledge.
verses.17: He arose and went away to the southern region.
verses.18: Yajnayajniya and Vamadevya and Sacrifice and Sacrificer and sacrificial victims followed him.
verses.19: The man who reviles the Vratya possessing this knowledge is alienated from Yajnayajniya and Vamadevya, Sacrifice, Sacrificer and sacrificial victims.
verses.20: He who hath this knowledge becomes the beloved home of Yajnayajniya,Vamadevya, Sacrifice, Sacrificer, and sacrificial victims.
verses.21: In the southern region Dawn is his leman, Mitra his panegyrist, knowledge his vesture, day his turban, night his hair, Indra's two Bays are his circular ornaments,
verses.22: New Moon Night and Full Moon Night are his running attendants, Mind, etc. as in stanza 1.
verses.23: Matarisvan and Pavamana are they who draw it, Vita is his charioteer, Storm his goad,
verses.24: Fame and Glory are his harbingers. Fame and Glory come to him who hath this knowledge.
verses.25: He arose and went away to the western region.
verses.26: Vairupa and Vairaja, the Waters, and King Varuna followed him.
verses.27: He who reviles the Vratya possessing this knowledge is alienated from Vairupa and Vairaja, the Waters and Varuna the King.
verses.28: He who possesses this knowledge becomes the dear home of Vairupa and Vairaja, the Waters and King Varuna.
verses.29: In the western region Ira is his leman, Laughter his panegyrist, knowledge, etc., as above.
verses.30: Day and Night are his running attendants, Mind, etc., as above.
verses.31: Matarisvan and Pavamana are they who draw it, Vita is his charioteer, Storm his goad,
verses.32: Fame and Glory are his harbingers. Fame and Glory come to him who hath this knowledge.
verses.33: He arose and went away to the northern region.
verses.34: Syaita and Naudhasa, the Seven Rishis, and King Soma followed him.
verses.35: He who reviles the Vratya possessing this knowledge is alienated from Syaita, etc.
verses.36: He who hath this knowledge becomes the dear home of Syaita, etc.
verses.37: In the northern region Lightning is his leman, thunder his panegyrist, etc. as above.
verses.38: Revelation and Tradition are his running attendants, Mind, etc., as above.
verses.39: Mātariśvan and Pavamāna the two drawers of the rough vehicle, the wind the charioteer, the whirlwind the goad,
verses.40: both fame and glory the two forerunners: to him cometh fame, cometh glory, who knoweth thus.
verses.41: For a whole year he stood erect. The Gods said unto him, Why standest thou, O Vratya? He answered and said, Let them bring my couch.
verses.42: He said: Let them bring together a settle āsandī́ for me.
verses.43: They brought the couch for that Vratya.
verses.44: Two of its feet were Summer and Spring, and two were Autumn and the Rains.
verses.45: Brihat and Rathantara were the two long boards, Yajnayajniya and Vamadevya the two cross-boards.
verses.46: Holy verses were the strings lengthwise, and Yajus formulas the cross-tapes.
verses.47: Sacred lore was the blanket, Devotion the coverlet.
verses.48: The Saman was the Cushion, and chanting the bolster.
verses.50: The hosts of Gods were his attendants, solemn vows his messengers, and all creatures his worshippers.
verses.51: All creatures become the worshippers of him who possesses this knowledge.
verses.52: For him they made the two Spring months protectors from the eastern region, and Brihat and Rathantara superintendents. The two Spring months protect from the eastern region, and Brihat and Rathantara superintend, the man who possesses this knowledge. For him they made the two Summer months protectors from the southern region, and Yajnayajniya and Vamadevya superintendents. The two Summer months, etc. as in Verse 1,
verses.53: For him, from the southern quarter, they made the two summer months guardians, and yajñāyajñíya and vāmadevyá attendants. The two summer months guard from the southern quarter, and yajñājñíya and vāmadevyá attend, him who knoweth thus.
verses.54: They made the two Rain months, his protectors from the western region, and Vairupa and Vairaja superintendents. The two Rain months, etc. as above.
verses.55: They made the two Autumn months his protectors from the northern region, and Syaita and Naudhasa superintendents. The two Autumn months. etc. as above.
verses.56: They made the two Winter months his protectors from the region of the nadir, and earth and Agni superintendents. The two Winter months, etc.
verses.57: They made the two Dewy months his protectors from the region of the zenith, and Heaven and the Adityas superintendents. The two Dewy months, etc.
verses.70: For him they made the Archer Bhava a deliverer from the intermediate space of the eastern region.
verses.71: Bhava the Archer, a deliverer, delivers him from the intermediate space of the eastern region.
verses.72: Neither Sarva nor Bhava nor Isana slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.73: They made Sarva the Archer his deliverer from the intermediate space of the southern region, etc, as in verse 1.
verses.74: They made Rudra the Archer his deliverer from the intermediate space of the region of the nadir etc.
verses.75: They made Mahādeva his deliverer from the intermediate space of the region of the zenith, etc.
verses.76: They made Pasupati the Archer his deliverer from the intermediate space of the western region, etc.
verses.77: The archer Paśupati attends him as attendant from the intermediate direction of the western quarter; not śarva etc. etc.
verses.78: Neither Sarva nor Bhava nor Isana slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.79: They made the Awful God, the Archer, his deliverer from the intermediate space of the northern region, etc, as above.
verses.80: The archer, the formidable god, attends him as attendant from the intermediate direction of the northern quarter; not śarva etc. etc.
verses.81: Neither Sarva nor Bhava nor Isana slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.82: They made Rudra the Archer his deliverer from the intermediate space of the region of the nadir etc.
verses.83: The archer Rudra attends him as attendant from the intermediate direction of the fixed quarter; not śarva etc. etc.
verses.84: Neither Sarva nor Bhava nor Isana slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.85: They made Mahadeva his deliverer from the intermediate space of the region of the zenith, etc.
verses.86: The archer Mahādeva attends him as attendant from the intermediate direction of the upward quarter; not śarva etc. etc.
verses.87: Neither Sarva nor Bhava nor Isana slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.88: ### Commentary 7. For him, from all the intermediate directions, they made the archer Īśāna attendant. ### Notes The mss. vary in *a and b between sárvebhyo ant- and -bhyo ‘nt-; in a, only P.M.W.E. have -bhyo ‘nt-; in b, at least two, E. and Bs. Probably our text ought to give in both places -bhyo ant-; so SPP. with all but two of his authorities. After the definition of the c of 1-7 the Anukr. adds: hinasti vyāghrādiṣv avagantavyaḥ; which apparently means that in 2-6 is to be understood the verb hinasti, which is expressed only in 1 c and 7 c; vyāghrādiṣu is probably a corruption. After its metrical definition of xi. 1. 36, the Anukr. inserts the words vyāghrādiṣv avagantavyā; and after that of xiv. 1. 60 occur the words (see p. 740) ity, or parāviny, edhiṣīmahīti vyāghrādiṣv avagantavyaḥ.—One ritual use of xiv. 1. 60 is as a prayer for the safety of the bride as she sets out for her new home. In that connection, a specification of the safety as "in respect of tigers and so forth" would be entirely appropriate. And it is also appropriate here, at xv. 5.—The verse xi. 1. 36 is used in the ritual (Kāuś. 63. 9) with iv. 14. 5 in the sava offering: the former, as a prayer for safety on the road to heaven (ágne patháḥ kalpaya devayā́nān) the latter, somewhat similarly (svàr yantu yájamānāḥ svastí*). Although tigers more frequently accelerate than retard a Hindu's transit to heaven, the verses may nevertheless be conceived as used secondarily for safety on terrestrial paths.—Accordingly the remark of the Anukr is perhaps intended as exegetical, but it is at any rate most unexpected.—The vs. AV. xii. 1. 49 furnishes testimony (quite superfluous) to the familiarity of the ancient Hindus with "man-eaters."
verses.89: Isana the Archer, a deliverer, delivers him from all the intermediate regions. Neither Sarva nor Bhava, nor Isana
verses.90: slays him who possesses this knowledge, or his cattle, or his kinsmen.
verses.91: He went his way to the region of the nadir.
verses.92: Earth and Agni and herbs and trees and shrubs and plants followed him.
verses.93: He who possesses this knowledge becomes the dear home of Earth and Agni and herbs and trees and shrubs and plants.
verses.94: He went his way to the region of the zenith.
verses.95: Right and Truth and Sun and Moon and Stars followed him.
verses.96: He who possesses this knowledge becomes, etc., as in verse 1. mutatis mutandis.
verses.97: He went away to the last region.
verses.98: Richas, Samans Yajus formulas and Devotion followed him.
verses.100: He went away to the great region.
verses.101: Itihasa and Purana and Gathas and Narasansis followed him.
verses.103: He went away to the supreme region.
verses.104: The Ehavaniya, Garhapatya, and Southern Fires, and Sacrifice, and Sacrificer, and sacrificial victims followed him.
verses.106: He went away to the unindicated region.
verses.107: The Seasons, groups of seasons, the worlds and their inhabitants, the months and half-months, and Day and Night followed him.
verses.109: He went away to the unfrequented region. Thence he thought that he should not return.
verses.110: Diti and Aditi and Ida and Indrani followed him.
verses.112: He went away to the regions.
verses.113: Viraj and all the Gods and all the Deities followed him.
verses.115: He went away to all the intermediate spaces.
verses.116: Prajapati and Parameshthin and the Father and the Great Father followed him.
verses.117: He who possesses this knowledge becomes the beloved home of Prajapati and Parameshthin and the Father and the Great Father.
verses.118: He, having become moving majesty, went to the ends of the earth. He became the sea.
verses.119: Prajapati and Parameshthin and the Father and the Great Father and the Waters and Faith, turned into rain, followed him.
verses.120: The Waters, Faith, and rain approach him who possesses this knowledge.
verses.121: Faith, and Sacrifice and the world, having become food and nourishment, turned toward him.
verses.122: Faith Sacrifice, the world, food and nourishment approach him who possesses this knowledge.
verses.123: He was filled with passion: from him sprang the Rajanya.
verses.124: He came to the people, to kinsmen, food and nourishment.
verses.125: He who possesses this knowledge becomes the dear home of the people, kinsmen, food and nourishment.
verses.126: He went away to the people.
verses.127: Meeting and Assembly and Army and Wine followed him.
verses.128: He who hath this knowledge becomes the dear home of Meeting, Assembly, Army, and Wine.
verses.129: So let the King, to whose house the Vratya who possesses this knowledge comes as a guest.
verses.130: Honour him as superior to himself. So he Both not act against the interests of his princely rank or his kingdom.
verses.131: From him, verily, sprang Priesthood and Royalty. They said, Into whom shall we enter?
verses.132: Let Priesthood enter into Brihaspati, and Royalty into Indra, was the answer.
verses.133: Hence Priesthood entered into Brihaspati and Royalty into Indra.
verses.134: Now this Earth is Brihaspati, and Heaven is Indra.
verses.135: Now this Agni is Priesthood, and yonder Sun is Royalty.
verses.136: Priesthood comes to him, and he becomes endowed with priestly lustre.
verses.137: Who knows that Earth is Brihaspati and Agni Priesthood.
verses.138: Great power comes to him and he becomes endowed with great power.
verses.139: Who knows that Aditya is Royalty and that Heaven is Indra.
verses.140: Let him to whose house the Vratya who possesses this knowledge comes as a guest.
verses.141: Rise up of his own accord to meet him, and say, Vratya, where didst thou pass the night? Vratya, here is water, Let them refresh thee. Vratya, let it be as thou pleasest. Vratya, as thy wish is so let it be. Vratya, as thy desire is so be it.
verses.142: When he says to his guest, Where didst thou pass the night? he reserves for himself thereby the paths that lead to the Gods.
verses.143: When he says to him, Here is water, he secures thereby water for himself.
verses.144: When he says to him, Let them refresh thee, he thereby wins vital breath to exceeding old age.
verses.145: When he says to him, Vratya, let it be as thou pleasest, he secures to himself thereby what is pleasant.
verses.146: That which is pleasant comes to him, and he is the beloved of the beloved, who is possessed of this knowledge.
verses.147: When he says to him, Vratya, as thy will is so let it be, he secures to himself thereby the fulfilment of his will.
verses.148: Authority comes to him who possesses this knowledge, and he becomes the controller of the powerful.
verses.149: When he says to him, Vratya, as thy desire is so be it, he secures to himself thereby the attainment of his desire.
verses.150: His desire comes to him who possesses this knowledge and he gains the complete satisfaction of his wish.
verses.151: The man, to whose house, when the fires have been taken up from the hearth and the oblation to Agni placed therein, the Vratya possessing this knowledge comes as a guest.
verses.152: Should of his own accord rise to meet him and say, Vratya, give me permission. I will sacrifice.
verses.153: And if he gives permission he should sacrifice, if he does not permit him he should not sacrifice.
verses.154: He who sacrifices when permitted by the Vratya who possesses this knowledge.
verses.155: Well knows the path that leads to the Fathers and the way that. leads to the Gods.
verses.156: He does not act in opposition to the Gods. It becomes his sacrifice.
verses.157: The abode of the man who sacrifices when permitted by the Vratya who possesses this knowledge is long left remaining in this world.
verses.158: But he who sacrifices without the permission of the Vratya whopossesses this knowledge.
verses.159: Knows not the path that leads to the Fathers nor the way that leads to the Gods.
verses.160: He is at variance with the Gods. He hath offered no accepted. sacrifice.
verses.161: The abode of the man who sacrifices without the permission of the Vratya who possesses this knowledge is not left remaining in this world.
verses.162: He in whose house the Vratya who possesses this knowledge abides one night secures for himself thereby the holy realms that are on earth.
verses.163: A second night . . . . the holy realms that are in the firmament (the rest as in verse 1).
verses.164: A third night . . . the holy realms that are in heaven.
verses.165: A fourth night . . . . the holy realms of the Holy.
verses.167: Now he to whose house a non-Vratya, calling himself a Vratya, and one in name only, comes as a guest.
verses.168: Should punish him and not punish him.
verses.169: He should serve him with food saying to himself, To this Deity I offer water: I lodge this Deity; I wait upon this, this Deity.
verses.170: To that Deity the sacrifice of him who has this knowledge is acceptable.
verses.176: He when he went away to the eastern region, went away having become the Marut host, and having made Mind an eater of food.
verses.177: He who hath this knowledge eats food with Mind as food-eater.
verses.178: He, when he went away to the southern region, went away having become Indra, and having made Strength an eater of food.
verses.179: He who hath this knowledge eats food with strength as food-eater.
verses.180: He, when he went away to the western region, went away having become King Varuna, and having made the Waters eaters of food.
verses.181: He who hath this knowledge eats food with the Waters as food-eaters.
verses.182: He, when he went away to the northern region, went away having become King Soma and having made the Seven Rishis' oblation an eater of food.
verses.183: He who hath this knowledge eats food with oblation as food-eater.
verses.184: He, when he went away to the stedfast region, went away having become Vishnu and having made Viraj an eater of food.
verses.185: He who hath this knowledge eats food with Viraj as food-eater.
verses.186: He, when he went away to animals, went away having become Rudra and having made herbs eaters of food.
verses.187: He who hath this knowledge eats food with herbs as food-eaters.
verses.188: He, when he went away to the Fathers, went away having become King Yama and having made the exclamation Svadha an eater of food.
verses.189: He who hath this knowledge eats food with the exclamation Svadha as food-eater.
verses.190: He, when he went away to men, went away having become Agni and having made the exclamation Svaha an eater of food.
verses.191: He who hath this knowledge eats food with the exclamation Svaha as food-eater.
verses.192: He, when he went away to the upper region, went away having become Brihaspati and having made the exclamation Vashat an eater of food.
verses.193: He who hath this knowledge eats food with the exclamation Vashat as food-eater.
verses.194: He, when he went away to the Gods, went away having become Isana and having made Passion an eater of food.
verses.195: He who hath this knowledge eats food with Passion as food-eater.
verses.196: He, when he went away to creatures, went away having become Prajapati and having made vital breath an eater of food.
verses.197: He who hath this knowledge eats food with vital breath as foodeater.
verses.198: He, when he went away to all the intermediate spaces, went away having become Parameshthin and having made Devotion an eater of food.
verses.199: He who hath this knowledge eats food with Devotion as food-eater.
verses.201: There are seven vital airs, seven downward breaths, seven diffused breaths.
verses.202: His first vital breath, called Upward, is this Agni.
verses.203: His second vital breath, called Mature, is that Aditya.
verses.204: His third vital breath, called Approached, is that Moon.
verses.205: His fourth vital breath, called Pervading is this Pavamana.
verses.206: His fifth vital breath, called Source, are these Waters.
verses.207: His sixth vital breath, called Dear, are these domestic animals.
verses.208: His seventh vital breath, called Unlimited, are these creatures.
verses.209: His first downward breath is the time of Full Moon.
verses.210: His second downward breath is the eighth day after Full Moon.
verses.211: His third downward breath is the night of New Moon.
verses.212: His fourth downward breath is Faith.
verses.213: His fifth downward breath is Consecration.
verses.214: His sixth downward breath is Sacrifice.
verses.215: His seventh downward breath are these sacrificial fees.
verses.216: His first diffused breath is this Earth.
verses.217: His second diffused breath is that Firmament.
verses.218: His third diffused breath is that Heaven.
verses.219: His fourth diffused breath are those Constellations.
verses.220: His fifth diffused breath are the Seasons.
verses.221: His sixth diffused breath are the Season-groups.
verses.222: His seventh diffused breath is the year.
verses.223: With one and the same object the Gods go round the Year and the Seasons follow round the Vratya.
verses.224: When they surround the Sun on the day of New Moon, and that time of Full Moon.
verses.225: That one immortality of theirs is just an oblation.
verses.227: The right eye is the Sun and the left eye is the Moon.
verses.228: His right ear is Agni and his left ear is Pavamana.
verses.229: Day and Night are his nostrils. Diti and Aditi are his head and skull.
verses.230: By day the Vratya is turned westward, by night he is turned eastward. Worship to the Vratya!
